name: OpenShell
description: OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for autonomous AI agents.
one_liner: A safety cage for AI agents — lets them read files, install software, and call APIs on a computer, but only within rules you set, so they can't leak your passwords or touch things they shouldn't.
buyer: A platform or DevOps lead at a mid-size company rolling out AI coding or ops agents in production, who needs to stop an agent from accidentally exfiltrating credentials or hitting the wrong server.
business_use_cases: A fintech runs its AI support agents inside OpenShell so they can query internal databases but are policy-blocked from ever reaching the public internet with customer data.
An agency running dozens of client coding agents locks each one to only that client's repo and API keys, so one compromised agent can't touch another client's secrets.
A SaaS company offers 'sandboxed agent hosting' to its enterprise customers as a compliance feature, built on OpenShell underneath.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a managed, hosted gateway with pre-built compliance policies (SOC2, HIPAA) for companies that don't want to run their own.
Sell enterprise support contracts and custom policy-authoring consulting to companies adopting agent fleets.

steal_this: This weekend, package OpenShell with a starter policy pack (no outbound internet except an allowlist, no /etc access) as a one-command 'safe agent sandbox' for indie developers running Claude Code or Codex overnight.
